Subject: docs/plan.md; revision 2f8aa08599b6d1181bf8891faf7d5260c87d4a90
Kind: plan
Serves: docs/requirements.md (accepted 2026-01-05): the stock report feels slow for operators with large files; make it faster.
Verification allowed: read-only, test execution, as authorized
Decision: go commits executing the plan as written — add buffering=1<<20 to the open() call in inventory/store.py load_items, then run the existing unit test suite; cost hours, one file edited plus one test run; two-way; blast radius inventory/store.py, its caller inventory/report.py, and operators running python3 -m inventory.report; owner Arlo Liu (requester)
Author: user; assessment independent; independent review not required
Criteria: in force 1,2,3,4,5,6; advisory 7; added none; waived before assessment none; sources defaults, repo rule AGENTS.md (run python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests before committing; stdlib only)
Steps:
- [S1] edit inventory/store.py load_items to pass buffering=1<<20 to open(); dependents: inventory/report.py (calls load_items), tests/test_store.py (tests load_items); two-way; handling: not required
- [S2] run python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests; dependents: none; two-way; handling: not required
Claims:
- [C1] reading the file in small chunks is the current bottleneck; relied on by S1; falsity surfaces at: no step in this plan; two-way; unverified; inventory/store.py:8 already opens the file with a buffered reader at Python's default buffer size, and no profiling data or large file exists in the repo to test whether raising the buffer size is what matters; the plan's own alternative section declines to profile
- [C2] the buffering change makes python3 -m inventory.report run measurably faster (the plan's stated Outcome); relied on by S1; falsity surfaces at: no step in this plan; two-way; unverified; S2 only runs the existing correctness tests (tests/test_store.py, tests/test_report.py) against data/items.csv, a 3-row file, with no timing assertion and no large file available to benchmark against
Verdict: no-go
Blockers:
- [B1] criterion 1; the plan's outcome ("the report runs faster") is never checked by any step — S2 is the ordinary correctness test suite run against a 3-row data/items.csv (confirmed passing at HEAD: 3 tests, ok), and the plan's own problem statement cites docs/requirements.md, a 5-line text file, as the "large file" example, so no large representative file and no timing step exist anywhere in the plan or repo; evidence: docs/plan.md lines 5 and 17-18, data/items.csv (3 rows), test run output (3 tests, ok, no timing); resolution: add a step that measures load_items or report runtime before and after the change on a representative large file, with a stated comparison or threshold, so "runs faster" is observable
Advisory: the alternative section rejects profiling as "unnecessary overhead for a small file," which sits oddly against the plan's own problem statement that the report is slow on large files — worth reconciling but not blocking
Not assessed: none
Later commitments: none
Pending owner confirmation: none
Owner override: none
Closing: no action follows from this report; a revised subject needs a new verdict
